- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review

I explored the codebase directly. Answers below.

---

**h01** — S3 presign runner (`s3presign.Runner`) — refreshes expiring presigned URLs for S3‑stored attachments — every 12 h plus once at startup — wired in `Server.startBackgroundRunners`.
- Component: `s3presign.Runner` / `Runner.CheckAndPresign` — `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:16`, `:47` (re‑presigns when the stored URL is within 4 days of its 5‑day expiry, `runner.go:88-92`)
- Schedule: `const runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12` ticker in `Runner.Run` — `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27,29-41`
- Wiring: `server/server.go:161-172` (`NewRunner` → immediate `RunOnce(ctx)` at `server/server.go:163`, then `go s3presignRunner.Run(s3Context)` at `:168`), called from `Server.Start` — `server/server.go:135`

**h02**
- Delivery function: `webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`; the actual HTTP round trip is `safeClient.Do(req)` at `internal/webhook/webhook.go:152`. It is normally reached asynchronously via `webhook.PostAsync` (`:184`) → bounded channel `asyncPostQueue` (`:39`) → 4 worker goroutines started in `init()` (`:42-55`).
- Protection: SSRF guard at dial time — `safeClient`'s `Transport.DialContext = safeDialContext` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:33-38`, `:59-83`), which resolves the host and rejects any answer in a reserved range via `isReservedIP` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:44-55`, CIDR list `:14-24`); this also defeats DNS rebinding. Second layer: `webhook.ValidateURL` at configuration time (scheme + resolved-IP check) — `internal/webhook/validate.go:62-88`. Escape hatch: the package-level `AllowPrivateIPs` flag — `internal/webhook/validate.go:41` (never set anywhere in the repo, so it defaults to `false`).

**h03**
- Abstraction package: `internal/idp` — `internal/idp/idp.go:1-8` (defines the shared `IdentityProviderUserInfo` contract; note it is a struct, not a Go interface — dispatch is a type switch on the stored config).
- Implementation package: `internal/idp/oauth2` — `internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go` (`IdentityProvider`, `NewIdentityProvider` at `:27`, `ExchangeToken`, `UserInfo`). It is the only one; selected at `server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go:120-121`.

**h04** — No.
- Evidence: `mysql.NewDB` appears exactly once in the repo, inside the factory: `store/db/db.go:22` (import at `store/db/db.go:8`, the only import of `github.com/usememos/memos/store/db/mysql` anywhere). By contrast `sqlite.NewDB` *is* constructed outside the factory, but only in tests (`store/demo_seed_test.go:24`, `store/deployment_config_test.go:416`). Test harnesses go through the factory too (`store/test/store.go:28,50`). The `mysql` identifier in `store/test/containers.go:20,42` is the testcontainers module, not the driver package.

**h05** — Explicit Go code, inside the driver's `DeleteUser` transaction. There is no DB-level cascade.
- Explicit deletes: `deleteReactionsByCreatorTx` (reactions the user made) and `deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx` (reactions on the user's memos) — `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:380-403`, `store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:380-402`, `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:417-439`
- No DB rule: the `reaction` table is declared with no FK/`ON DELETE CASCADE` in any dialect — `store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:91-99`, `store/migration/postgres/LATEST.sql:91-98`, `store/migration/mysql/LATEST.sql:90-98`. The only `FOREIGN KEY … ON DELETE CASCADE` in the current schema is `memo_share.memo_id` (`store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:109`).
- Entry point: `Store.DeleteUser` → `s.driver.DeleteUser` — `store/user.go:171-172`

**h06** — Handlers (all in `server/router/api/v1`):
- `CreateMemo` — `memo_service.go:70` → `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` at `memo_service.go:157`
- `UpdateMemo` — `memo_service.go:401` → `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` at `memo_service.go:513` → `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` at `memo_update_helpers.go:67`
- `DeleteMemo` — `memo_service.go:518` → `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` at `memo_service.go:562`
- `CreateMemoComment` — `memo_service_comments.go:20` → `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` at `memo_service_comments.go:119`
- also `SetMemoRelations` (`memo_relation_service.go:48`) and `SetMemoAttachments` (`memo_attachment_service.go:48`), both via `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects`

Convergence function: `webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120` (all paths funnel through `webhook.PostAsync`, `internal/webhook/webhook.go:184`, whose workers call `Post`).

**h07**
- `serveUserAvatar` (route `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar`) — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:167` (registered at `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:124`)
- `FileServerService.getUserByUsername` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715-717`
- `Store.GetUser` (checks `userCache` by ID first) — `store/user.go:148-169`
- `Store.ListUsers` (populates `userCache`) — `store/user.go:136-146`
- `Driver.ListUsers` (interface) — `store/driver.go:47`
- `(*DB).ListUsers` — `store/db/sqlite/user.go:88` (default install; `store/db/postgres/user.go`, `store/db/mysql/user.go:147` for the other dialects)
- Then back in the handler: `parseDataURI(user.AvatarURL)` decodes the stored `data:` URI and `c.Blob` writes it — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:196-208`, `:736-742`. The avatar bytes live in the `user.avatar_url` column, not on disk.

**h08** — Two declarers:
- `*s3presign.Runner.RunOnce` — `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:43` — invoked: **yes** — `server/server.go:163` (startup) and `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:36` (12 h ticker)

- Concrete: `*SSEHub.Close` `server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:99`; `*Store.Close` `store/store.go:72`; `*cache.Cache.Close` `store/cache/cache.go:187`; `*sqlite.DB.Close` `store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go:67`; `*postgres.DB.Close` `store/db/postgres/postgres.go:46`; `*mysql.DB.Close` `store/db/mysql/mysql.go:47`
- Interface declarations: `store.Driver.Close` `store/driver.go:12`; `cache.Interface.Close` `store/cache/cache.go:31`

Invoked from non-test server code:
- `*Store.Close` ← `server/server.go:146` (`Server.Shutdown`)
- `*SSEHub.Close` ← `server/server.go:206` (`closeLongLivedConnections`)
- `*cache.Cache.Close` ← `store/store.go:74-76` (three caches)
- `*sqlite.DB.Close` ← via the `Driver` interface at `store/store.go:78`; `postgres`/`mysql` `Close` only run when those drivers are selected (`store/db/db.go:20-25`)

**h10** — `(*renderer).addArg` — `internal/filter/render.go:842` — ~28 call sites (all within `internal/filter/render.go`; verified by counting `addArg(` occurrences minus the declaration). Runner‑up: `Schema.Field` — `internal/filter/schema.go:67` — 19 call sites across `internal/filter/parser.go` and `render.go`. (Counts are non‑test call sites; method names like `Next`/`Validate`/`Parse` produce larger raw grep counts but those hits belong to unrelated receivers, e.g. `sql.Rows.Next`.)

**h11** — Counting packages outside `store/…` that reference the type:
- 1st: `store.User` — ~7 packages (`server/auth`, `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/fileserver`, `server/router/frontend`, `server/router/rss`)

By raw reference count the order inverts (`store.Memo` ≈ 150 refs vs `store.User` ≈ 119), but by *package* breadth `User` leads. Type declarations: `store/user.go:29`, `store/memo.go`.

**h12**
- Concrete method: `(*sqlite.DB).CreateMemo` — `store/db/sqlite/memo.go:16` (the `INSERT INTO \`memo\` … RETURNING …` statement is built at `store/db/sqlite/memo.go:41-42`)
- Determination: the default for the `driver` flag/config is `"sqlite"` — `cmd/memos/main.go:122` (`viper.SetDefault("driver", "sqlite")`) and `:130` (flag default). That value lands in `Profile.Driver` (`cmd/memos/main.go:43`), which the factory switches on: `store/db/db.go:19-26` picks `sqlite.NewDB`. The resulting `store.Driver` is injected once via `store.New(dbDriver, …)` (`cmd/memos/main.go:57-64`, `store/store.go:37`), and `Store.CreateMemo` delegates straight to it (`store/memo.go:109-114`). So the interface has three implementations (`sqlite`, `postgres`, `mysql`) but only one is ever bound per process, fixed at startup — sqlite by default. `Profile.Driver == "sqlite"` also drives the default DSN `memos_prod.db` (`internal/profile/profile.go:110-117`).

**h13**
- Implementation: exactly one — the unexported `*markdown.service` — `internal/markdown/markdown.go:57-60` (sole `ExtractAll` implementor, `internal/markdown/markdown.go:356`)
- Construction: `markdown.NewService(...)` — `internal/markdown/markdown.go:85`; the only production call site is `NewAPIV1Service` at `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48-51`, with `WithTagExtension()` and `WithMentionExtension()`
- Holders of the `markdown.Service` interface: `APIV1Service.MarkdownService` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:35`); `RSSService.MarkdownService` (`server/router/rss/rss.go:45`, handed the same instance at `server/server.go:85`); `memopayload.Runner.MarkdownService` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:16` — declared but never constructed in production); plus `RebuildMemoPayload`, which takes it as a parameter (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74`)

- `checkMemoReadAccess` (single-memo read: archived + PRIVATE/PROTECTED) — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:39-67`
- `ListMemos` visibility narrowing (anonymous → PUBLIC only; other-user → PUBLIC+PROTECTED) — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:217-227`

- File server `checkAttachmentPermission` (incl. anonymous policy and `share_token` bypass) — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:670-703`
- RSS feeds restricted to PUBLIC — `server/router/rss/rss.go:90` and `:141`

---

**r01** — Premise is wrong: there is no Redis anywhere in the codebase (no `redis` import in `go.mod`, no matches in any `.go` file). Caching is a hand-rolled in-process map: `store/cache/cache.go` (`Cache`, `Interface` at `:10-31`), with three instances on `Store` — `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache` (`store/store.go:26-29`, created at `store/store.go:47-49`). The user-entry TTL is the shared `DefaultTTL` of **10 minutes**, with a 5‑minute cleanup sweep and a 1000‑item cap — `store/store.go:38-43` (mirrored in `cache.DefaultConfig`, `store/cache/cache.go:55-60`). Cache writes/invalidations: `store/user.go:143,167` and `store/user_delete.go:39-46`.

**r02** — Premise is wrong: there is no rate-limiting middleware, per-user or otherwise. A case-insensitive search for `ratelimit`/`rate_limit`/`limiter`/`throttle` across all Go sources returns nothing. The only Echo middleware registered is `middleware.Recover()` and the CORS middleware — `server/server.go:51-52`. The auth/authorization interceptors (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:66-90`, `connect_interceptors.go`, `authz.go`) do authentication and access policy only, with no request counting. The closest things to limits are concurrency semaphores for thumbnail/image work (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:59-60`, `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:107`) and a 256 MiB body cap (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:20`).

**r03** — Premise is wrong: there is no cron scheduler running any job, and no nightly database-cleanup job. `internal/scheduler` is a cron library that exists in the tree but is **never instantiated by production code** — every reference to `scheduler.New`/`Register` outside the package itself is in `internal/scheduler/doc.go` comments or `_test.go` files. The only scheduled background work in the server is the S3 presign runner on a 12‑hour `time.Ticker` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27-41`, wired at `server/server.go:161-172`) — an interval, not a wall-clock time, and it presigns URLs rather than cleaning up.

**r04** — Premise is wrong: neither NATS nor RabbitMQ is used; there is no message broker and no queue declaration in the codebase. Webhook delivery is entirely in-process: a buffered Go channel `asyncPostQueue` of capacity 128 (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`) drained by **4 goroutines** started in `init()` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55`). Producers call `webhook.PostAsync`, which does a non-blocking send and **drops** the delivery with a warning if the buffer is full (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:184-196`). Each worker calls `Post` (`:120`), which POSTs via the SSRF-guarded `safeClient` with a 30 s timeout (`:31-38`, `:152`). Consequence: queued webhooks are lost on restart and there is no retry.

**r05** — Premise is wrong: there is no GraphQL schema, server, or dependency (no `gqlgen`/`graphql` in `go.mod` or any source file). The public API is **protobuf/gRPC-based**, exposed three ways over a single Echo HTTP server:
- Connect-RPC handlers — `server/router/api/v1/connect_handler.go`, `connect_services.go`, generated stubs in `proto/gen/api/v1/apiv1connect/`
- gRPC-Gateway REST/JSON transcoding — registered by `APIV1Service.RegisterGateway`, `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:64+`, generated `*.pb.gw.go` under `proto/gen/api/v1/`
- Service definitions in `proto/api/v1/*.proto` (memo, user, auth, attachment, instance, shortcut, idp, ai)

Plus non-RPC surfaces: `/file/...` (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121-125`), RSS (`server/router/rss/rss.go`), MCP (`server/router/mcp/`), and `/healthz` (`server/server.go:64`).
